changes.comment: A folder someone shares out of a vault you also have becomes a shared folder on your copy too, by itself and within seconds — the notes stay exactly where they are on disk, keep their history, and are never re-downloaded or duplicated.

A device that was closed while the folder was shared catches up the next time it opens, and a device interrupted halfway through — even by a crash — finishes the job on its next start rather than leaving notes in two places.
A shared folder you hold no link for still works: its notes stay on disk, open and edit normally, and start syncing the moment the link is added — nothing is re-downloaded and no file is touched.
When the person who shared a folder stops sharing it, your copy folds it back into the vault with its notes intact and their history unbroken.
Adding a shared folder to a vault that is itself synced now works, and the other devices on that vault are told about it.
Edits made while a folder was being shared are no longer lost in the changeover: whatever a note holds at that moment travels into the shared folder with it.
Renames, deletions and new files that arrive for a folder that has just become shared are replayed inside it instead of being dropped — and a big batch of deletions still waits for your confirmation.
